## section: teleport-from-cli-to-web
    Teleport from CLI to web
    cite: https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/teleport-cli-web
# Teleport from CLI to web

Teleport moves a CLI session into a **Vibe Code Web sandbox** so the task can keep running without your terminal staying open. Use it when a task is long, when you want to follow it from another device, or when you want the agent to push commits and open a pull request from the cloud.

> **Info**
>
> Teleport is part of the Vibe Code Web sandbox flow, currently in **Public Preview**. Capabilities, limits, and the interface can change before general availability.

## section: prerequisites
    Teleport from CLI to web > Prerequisites
    cite: https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/teleport-cli-web#prerequisites
## Prerequisites {#prerequisites}

Before you teleport, make sure that:

- You use an API key tied to a **Pro, Team, or Enterprise** account.
- The **[Mistral GitHub App](https://github.com/apps/mistralai/installations/new)** is installed on the repository you're working in.
- Your local session runs on a **Mistral model** (for example, Mistral Medium 3.5 or Devstral). Sessions on third-party models cannot be teleported.
- You run the CLI from inside a **Git repository**.

Upgrade to the latest CLI before you start:

```bash
uv tool upgrade mistral-vibe
```

## section: single-prompt
    Teleport from CLI to web > Two ways to use Teleport > Send a single prompt to a cloud session
    cite: https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/teleport-cli-web#single-prompt
### Send a single prompt to a cloud session {#single-prompt}

From inside a Git repository, prefix any prompt with `&`:

```bash
vibe
> & fix the failing tests
```

The task runs in a cloud sandbox. The CLI returns a Vibe Code Web URL where you can follow the session.

## section: move-session
    Teleport from CLI to web > Two ways to use Teleport > Move an in-progress local session to the cloud
    cite: https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/teleport-cli-web#move-session
### Move an in-progress local session to the cloud {#move-session}

Inside an active local session, run:

```text
/teleport
```

The session continues in Vibe Code Web, powered by Mistral Medium 3.5. You can monitor it from any device signed in to Vibe.

## section: what-happens
    Teleport from CLI to web > What happens after Teleport
    cite: https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/teleport-cli-web#what-happens
## What happens after Teleport {#what-happens}

When the cloud session runs, the agent typically:

1. **Clones your repository** into the sandbox.
2. **Works through the task**: reads files, runs commands, edits code.
3. **Streams progress** into Vibe Code Web in real time.
4. **Asks clarifying questions** when needed.
5. **Pushes a branch and opens a draft pull request** when done.

Commits, branches, and pull requests created during the run stay in your repository. The sandbox is deleted when the session ends.

## section: limits
    Teleport from CLI to web > Limits
    cite: https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/teleport-cli-web#limits
## Limits {#limits}

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Maximum session duration | 24 hours |
| Inactivity timeout (waiting for your reply) | 3 hours |
| Individual command timeout | 30 seconds |
| Concurrent sessions per user | Plan-dependent |

## section: caveats
    Teleport from CLI to web > Known caveats
    cite: https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/teleport-cli-web#caveats
## Known caveats {#caveats}

- **Teleport is one-way.** Once a session moves to the cloud, you can't pull it back into the local CLI. Continue from Vibe Code Web.
- **Only works from inside a Git repository.** Running it from a non-code directory fails.
- **Cloud sessions run on Mistral Medium 3.5**, regardless of the local model.

## section: choose-cli-vs-code-or-web-sessions
    Choose CLI, VS Code, or web sessions
    cite: https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/choose-cli-vscode-web-sessions
# Choose CLI, VS Code, or web sessions

**One agent, three surfaces.** Vibe Code runs as the CLI, the VS Code extension, and Vibe Code Web. They share the same engine, configuration, and customization layer (agents, skills, MCP servers), so you can pick whichever fits the task at hand.

> **Info**
>
> Vibe also implements the [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](https://agentclientprotocol.com/) and is published in the [ACP registry](https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/registry/tree/main/mistral-vibe), so you can run it in other [ACP-compatible clients](https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/clients), including JetBrains IDEs. For setup steps, see [Use Vibe in other IDEs](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/use-vibe-in-other-ides). This page focuses on the supported surfaces.

## section: get-started
    Choose CLI, VS Code, or web sessions > Get started
    cite: https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/choose-cli-vscode-web-sessions#get-started
## Get started {#get-started}

**CLI**

**Pick the CLI when you want Vibe directly in your terminal.**

The CLI is the most flexible surface. It runs in any terminal emulator, supports interactive sessions and scripting, and has full access to your shell and working tree.

Typical tasks:

- *"Refactor `src/api/handlers/` to use the new error handler pattern."*
- *"Explain how authentication works in this repo."*
- *"Run the test suite, fix what fails, and commit the result."*
- Scripted or unattended runs with `vibe --prompt` for CI and automation.

[Get started with the CLI](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/install-setup)

**VS Code extension**

**Pick the VS Code extension when you want Vibe in your editor.**

You don't need to install the CLI. The extension gives you access to all CLI capabilities through the [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com/), and adds **editor context** on top: active file, selection, diffs, and source control, all in the same workspace.

Typical tasks:

- *"Explain the file I'm currently looking at."*
- *"Review this diff for edge cases before I open a pull request."*
- *"Refactor this selection to make error handling explicit."*

[Get started with the VS Code extension](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/vs-code-extension/install-authenticate)

**Vibe Code Web**

**Pick Vibe Code Web for a cloud session on a GitHub repository, straight from your browser.**

No local checkout required. Vibe Code Web runs in a managed sandbox, works directly against a GitHub repository, and can prepare branches and pull requests for you.

Typical tasks:

- *"Inspect and change a repo I don't have cloned locally."*
- *"Prepare a branch and open a PR from a remote session."*
- *"Continue the session I started in the CLI on the web."*
- Let an agent work autonomously on your codebase while you do something else.

[Get started with Vibe Code Web](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/vibe-code-web/get-started)

[Get started with Vibe Code Web](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/vibe-code-web/get-started)

> **Tip**
>
> **CLI and VS Code extension share the same configuration and sessions** (agents, skills, MCP servers, profiles, and conversation history). You can start a session in the CLI and resume it in the extension, or the other way around, without losing context.
>
> To hand off work to Vibe Code Web, use the `/teleport` command from the CLI. See the [dedicated article](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/teleport-cli-web) for the current flow and limits.

## What each surface gives you {#what-each-surface-gives-you}

| | CLI | VS Code extension | Vibe Code Web |
|---|---|---|---|

- **Direct GitHub repository access** (CLI requires a local clone)

- **Managed cloud session lifetime** (CLI sessions are tied to your local terminal)
- **No local install required** (CLI requires a local install)
